title: The Download: Chinese AI divides the White House, and a record copyright payout

paragraphs.text: This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
paragraphs.translation: 這是今日版的 The Download，我們的平日電子報，為您提供科技界的每日動態。

paragraphs.text: China’s AI models have Trump’s AI world at war with itself
paragraphs.translation: 中國的 AI 模型讓川普的 AI 圈陷入內鬥

paragraphs.text: Last weekend, several current and former advisers to President Donald Trump on AI publicly lobbed insults at the country’s leading AI companies. David Sacks branded Anthropic’s models “lobotomized” and “woke.” Emil Michael, a top Pentagon official, called OpenAI’s new head of strategic futures a “supreme village idiot.”
paragraphs.translation: 上週末，幾位現任及前任川普的 AI 顧問公開羞辱該國領先的 AI 公司。David Sacks 稱 Anthropic 的模型為「被切除腦葉的」且「覺醒（woke）」。前五角大廈官員 Emil Michael 稱 OpenAI 的新任策略未來負責人為「終極村中白痴」。

paragraphs.text: It began because no one can agree on what to do about Kimi, a free, open-source model that Chinese AI company Moonshot launched last week. It appears to rival the intelligence of models from OpenAI and Anthropic, which are very much not free.
paragraphs.translation: 這起爭議源於大家對如何處理 Kimi 意見不一。Kimi 是中國 AI 公司月之暗面（Moonshot）上週推出的免費開源模型。它的智慧程度似乎足以與 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 的模型匹敵，而後兩者的模型並非免費。

paragraphs.text: Every time a new smart, free model from China gets released, US companies see less reason to fork out money for models from Anthropic or OpenAI. That’s creating economic and political problems for the president—and dividing the top AI strategists in his orbit.
paragraphs.translation: 每當中國發布新的智慧、免費模型時，美國企業就越沒有動力花錢購買 Anthropic 或 OpenAI 的模型。這給總統帶來了經濟與政治問題，並使他周圍的頂尖 AI 策略家產生分歧。

paragraphs.text: Read the full story on why no one can agree what to do about Kimi.
paragraphs.translation: 閱讀全文，了解為何眾人對如何處理 Kimi 難以達成共識。

paragraphs.text: I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.
paragraphs.translation: 我搜尋了網路，為您找出了今日最有趣、最重要、最可怕且最引人入勝的科技報導。

paragraphs.text: 1 Anthropic's record $1.5 billion copyright settlement has been approved The plaintiffs said Anthropic used pirated works to train Claude. (Reuters $) + And won the largest known copyright payout in history. (Engadget) + Yet many authors and creators still don’t view it as a win. (TechCrunch) + But AI copyright anxiety could limit creativity. (MIT Technology Review) 2 The Trump administration is weighing a ban on Chinese AI models The launch of Kimi K3 has revived calls for restrictions. (Axios) + But officials are divided on the proposals. (Fast Company) + China’s bet on open-source is paying off. (MIT Technology Review) 3 China is mulling tighter export controls on AI models and chips It wants to stop the West from acquiring its tech and startups. (FT $) + Beijing has held talks with tech firms about potential restrictions. (Reuters $) 4 Trump’s AI safety head has resigned after just three months Chris Fall had led CAISI, the federal AI Safety Institute, since April. (Axios) + No reason was given for his exit. (CNBC) 5 Google is working on a new chip to run Gemini models more efficiently The chip, called “Frozen V2,” may be deployed in 2028. (Information $) + Alphabet stock popped on the report. (CNBC) 6 New Orleans police have explored arming drones with weapons A draft drone manual paves the way for weaponised quadcopters. (404 Media) + Shoplifters could soon be chased by drones. (MIT Technology Review) 7 The EU has handed AliExpress a record fine over unsafe product sales The €550 million fine is the largest-ever under the Digital Services Act. (BBC) + Alibaba has vowed to appeal the fine. (SCMP) 8 Election advice from AI chatbots is “inaccurate and unreliable” That’s the conclusion from tests in Hungary earlier this year. (Guardian) 9 Red light therapy is showing promise for healing and healthy aging Better skin and reduced vision loss are also on the cards. (Economist $) 10 Neill Blomkamp’s new horror clip is all AI-generated—and it sucks The acclaimed director wants to make “a full feature in this format.” (Gizmodo)
paragraphs.translation: 1 Anthropic 創紀錄的 15 億美元版權和解協議獲批。原告稱 Anthropic 使用盜版作品訓練 Claude。並贏得了歷史上已知的最大版權賠付。然而，許多作家和創作者仍不認為這是一場勝利。但 AI 版權焦慮可能會限制創意。2 川普政府正考慮禁止中國 AI 模型。Kimi K3 的推出再次引發了限制呼聲。但官員們對提案意見分歧。中國在開源上的賭注正在產生回報。3 中國正考慮加強 AI 模型與晶片的出口管制。它希望阻止西方獲取其技術與新創公司。北京已與科技公司就潛在限制進行了會談。4 川普的 AI 安全負責人在任職僅三個月後辭職。Chris Fall 自四月起領導聯邦 AI 安全研究所 CAISI。未給出離職原因。5 Google 正開發新晶片以更高效地運行 Gemini 模型。該晶片名為「Frozen V2」，可能於 2028 年部署。Alphabet 股價在報告發布後上漲。6 紐奧良警方探索為無人機裝備武器。無人機手冊草案為武裝四軸飛行器鋪平了道路。扒手可能很快就會被無人機追捕。7 歐盟因銷售不安全產品對全球速賣通（AliExpress）處以創紀錄罰款。5.5 億歐元的罰款是《數位服務法》下有史以來最大的一筆。阿里巴巴誓言對罰款提出上訴。8 來自 AI 聊天機器人的選舉建議「不準確且不可靠」。這是今年早些時候在匈牙利進行測試得出的結論。9 紅光療法在癒合和健康老化方面展現前景。改善皮膚和減少視力喪失也在預期之內。10 尼爾·布隆坎普的新恐怖片段全是 AI 生成的——而且很爛。這位知名導演想用這種格式拍攝「一部完整的長片」。

paragraphs.text: Inside Chicago’s surveillance panopticon
paragraphs.translation: 深入芝加哥的監控全景監獄

paragraphs.text: Early on the morning of September 2, 2024, four people were shot and killed on a westbound train in Chicago. Police swiftly activated a digital dragnet—a surveillance network that connects thousands of cameras across the city—and arrested the suspect just 90 minutes later.
paragraphs.translation: 2024 年 9 月 2 日清晨，四人在芝加哥一列往西行駛的火車上遭槍擊身亡。警方迅速啟動了數位搜捕網——一個連接全市數千台攝影機的監控網絡——並在短短 90 分鐘後逮捕了嫌疑人。

paragraphs.text: Law enforcement and security advocates say this vast monitoring system protects public safety and works well. But activists and many residents say it's a surveillance panopticon that creates a chilling effect on behavior and violates guarantees of privacy and free speech.
paragraphs.translation: 執法部門和安全倡導者表示，這個龐大的監測系統保護了公共安全且運作良好。但活動人士和許多居民表示，這是一個全景監獄（panopticon），對行為產生了寒蟬效應，並違反了隱私和言論自由的保障。
